newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower as central bank steps in.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower as central bank steps in.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar after the central Bank of Korea (BOK) intervened to support the local currency, dealers said on Tuesday.
But the BOK has never confirmed interventing.
Dealers said the central bank intervened in the market twice after the won fell to a low of 830.00.
The won closed at 829.10 after opening at 829.80. It hit an intra-day high of 828.00.
"The central bank was seen selling about $300 million until the won recovered to the 828.40 level but the amount was almost matched with importer deals," said a foreign bank dealer.
"As dealers remained bullish toward the dollar, late short-covering pushed the greenback up before the close," said a local bank dealer.
Dealers said the dollar would test the 830 level tomorrow.

"The central bank is unlikely to support the won tomorrow because it has been too actively intervening lately. I cannot rule out the possibility for the dollar to touch a high of 835," the local bank dealer said.
Dealers forecast Wednesday's mid-rate would be pegged at 828.60 against 829.50 today. They said the market would move in a 828.00-829.50 range. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
